subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Burj Khalifa: Engineering the World's Tallest Building
description: A quick win: understand The Burj Khalifa: Engineering the World's Tallest Building.

hook.text: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai stands 2,717 feet tall. It's so tall that sunset happens two minutes later at the top than at the base.

buildup.text: The Y-shaped floor plan acts as a buttressed core. Each wing supports the others, reducing wind load on the structure.

discovery.text: The foundation sits on 192 concrete piles driven 164 feet into the ground. In Dubai's soft sand, deep foundations are essential.

twist.text: Pumping concrete to the 160th floor required special mixtures that stayed fluid for three hours during the long vertical journey.

climax.text: The exterior cladding has 26,000 glass panels. Each was individually designed to handle wind pressures that vary by height.

punchline.text: So tall the sunset takes longer at the top. Engineering bent time.

quiz.question: Why does the Burj Khalifa use a Y-shaped floor plan?
options: The shape maximizes the number of apartment units with corner views
Each wing buttresses the others, reducing wind load on the structure
The Y-shape allows three separate elevator banks for faster access
